title: M-C Pressure Clock
lede: Register six → read their six → bring the three that attacks their structure. Mega Salamence is the clock; Rotom-Wash buys the turn; Kingambit closes.
philosophy: Treat the six as a preview toolbox, not a fixed team. Mega Salamence is the primary win condition when they lack a clean Flying answer. Rotom-Wash burns and Volt Switches into free entries. Kingambit closes with Supreme Overlord and priority. Rillaboom, Mimikyu, and Focus Sash Garchomp replace pieces when the preview demands it. Do not always bring the same three.
meta: Regulation M-C runs from September 9, 2026 through December 2, 2026. Singles uses a six-Pokemon registration, 90-second preview, and three-Pokemon selection at level 50. Mega Evolution is available once per battle, and Mega Salamence is newly available in M-C. The six uses Mega Salamence as its dedicated Mega threat while the other five retain independent value when Salamence is not selected.
setsNote: Every Pokémon has exactly 66 SP with no stat above 32. Mega Salamence holds Salamencite — the only Mega on the six. Items are unique. Default Garchomp is four-attacks Focus Sash: Earthquake, Dragon Claw, Rock Slide, Fire Fang. Select from the six by preview; the core is a teaching default, not a mandatory trio.

Preserve Salamence if it is your only reliable route through the opponent's remaining structure.

packs.label: Core Clock
packs.when: Their six has no single structure that hard-invalidates Salamence, Rotom-Wash, and Kingambit together.
packs.identity: Balanced pivot into Mega Salamence setup and Kingambit cleanup.

strategy.opponentPattern: Their six is structurally balanced and does not clearly invalidate Salamence, Rotom-Wash, or Kingambit.
strategy.purpose: Use Rotom-Wash to control tempo, Salamence to create the primary offensive threat, and Kingambit to close once the opponent is weakened.
targets: Physical offense without a clean Rotom-Wash answer
Teams relying on slower Steel or Ground structures
Teams that struggle to prevent Salamence from setting up
refuses: Do not bring this package when the opponent has multiple strong answers to Salamence and Kingambit simultaneously.
Do not bring this package when Rotom-Wash is obviously overloaded by the opposing six.
strategy.winCondition: Create one safe Salamence setup opportunity or use Rotom-Wash to chip and pivot until Kingambit can clean.

pilot.thesis: Make the opponent answer Salamence without exposing Kingambit until the endgame.
pilot.rule: Do not trade your defensive pivot for early chip unless the trade opens Salamence or Kingambit.
pilot.fail: If Salamence cannot set up and Rotom-Wash cannot maintain tempo, stop forcing the default plan and choose a different pack next battle.

packs.meta: This is the baseline package for learning the team's decision structure. It is not a mandatory trio.
packs.philosophy: Rotom-Wash buys turns, Salamence converts a safe turn into pressure, and Kingambit turns accumulated damage into a finish.
press: Make them reveal their Salamence answer before committing to Mega Evolution.
Force physical attackers to respect Will-O-Wisp.
Preserve Kingambit until priority becomes decisive.
refuse: Never Mega Salamence merely because you brought it.
Never spend Kingambit early just to remove a target that another teammate can handle.
Never leave Rotom-Wash in front of an obvious super-effective attack merely to maintain momentum.

switches.send: Rotom-Wash to reduce physical pressure and create a pivot.
Kingambit to threaten with Steel STAB and resist the opposing Fairy pressure.
Salamence when its Ground immunity is safe and the opponent cannot immediately punish the switch.

plan.title: Clock
plan.goal: Establish which opposing Pokémon is responsible for stopping Salamence.
plan.play: Use Rotom-Wash to scout, burn, or Volt Switch while avoiding unnecessary damage.
plan.next: Once the Salamence answer is weakened or forced out, prepare the setup turn.

plan.title: Shield
plan.goal: Keep Salamence and Kingambit out of avoidable revenge ranges.
plan.play: Use Rotom-Wash as the defensive buffer and refuse unnecessary all-in trades.
plan.next: When the opponent's faster threats are weakened, transition to Salamence or Kingambit.

plan.title: Clean
plan.goal: Finish with the remaining offensive win condition.
plan.play: Mega Salamence sweeps if its checks are gone; otherwise preserve Salamence and let Kingambit clean.
plan.next: Use Sucker Punch when the opponent must attack and Kowtow Cleave when they can safely refuse.

loops.title: Volt Switch Loop
loops.body: Threaten Hydro Pump or Will-O-Wisp, force the opponent to respect the threat, then Volt Switch into the breaker that attacks their chosen response.

loops.title: Intimidate Loop
loops.body: Use Salamence's pre-Mega Intimidate to reduce physical pressure, then preserve the Mega until the opponent's answer has been identified.

victims.name: Physical attackers
victims.why: Rotom-Wash can burn them while Salamence and Kingambit exploit the reduced pressure.

victims.name: Balanced slower teams
victims.why: They can struggle to prevent Dragon Dance Salamence or Swords Dance Kingambit from becoming the final threat.

victims.name: Water and Ground cores
victims.why: Rotom-Wash can pressure them while Salamence supplies a Ground immunity.

counters.name: Multiple dedicated Salamence answers
counters.why: Bring the anti-structure pack instead, especially the Garchomp package.

counters.name: Heavy special offense
counters.why: Bring the special-spam package with Rillaboom instead.

advantages.title: Three independent win paths
advantages.body: Salamence can sweep, Kingambit can clean, and Rotom-Wash can generate the turns that let either one function.
advantages.watch: Do not assume all three must survive.
advantages.play: Identify which two are actually needed after preview.
advantages.rule: Sacrifice the least important piece only when it opens the correct win condition.

advantages.title: Tempo without recklessness
advantages.body: Volt Switch gives the team a way to turn defensive positioning into offensive positioning.
advantages.play: Use the threat of Hydro Pump or Will-O-Wisp to make the pivot meaningful.
advantages.rule: Pivot because the opponent's response is predictable, not because Volt Switch is available.

hazards.title: Ice pressure
hazards.body: Salamence and Garchomp are both vulnerable to Ice attacks, so preview any strong Ice attacker before selecting them.
hazards.watch: Never assume Salamence can safely switch into a known Ice attack.
hazards.play: Use Rotom-Wash or Kingambit to absorb the appropriate pressure when possible.
hazards.rule: Do not select both Dragon attackers when the opponent has multiple reliable Ice answers unless their coverage is otherwise exploitable.

hazards.title: Fairy pressure
hazards.body: Dragon attacks are unreliable into Fairy targets, making Kingambit's Steel STAB important.
hazards.watch: Track every Fairy Pokémon before committing Salamence or Garchomp.
hazards.play: Use Kingambit to pressure Fairy targets and preserve it when they are central to the opponent's plan.
hazards.rule: Do not throw away Kingambit early if it is your only clean Fairy answer.

phases.title: Preview
phases.lede: Find the opponent's Salamence answer and identify which of your three Pokémon can exploit it.

branches.when: Their six is balanced and Rotom-Wash has useful defensive targets.
branches.why: The default structure has the fewest forced assumptions.

branches.when: They show multiple physical attackers but lack strong special pressure.
branches.then: Still consider the core, but plan Rotom-Wash as the main shield.
branches.why: Burn and pivoting can dismantle their physical structure.

branches.when: They show several hard Salamence answers.
branches.then: Switch to a package containing Garchomp or Mimikyu instead.
branches.why: Do not force the Mega into a preview where its win condition is structurally denied.

phases.title: Lead
phases.lede: Use Rotom-Wash when you need information and tempo; use Salamence or Kingambit only when the matchup is immediately favorable.

branches.when: The opposing lead is a physical attacker that Rotom-Wash can safely disrupt.
branches.why: Remove pressure or create the first favorable transition.

branches.when: The opposing lead cannot threaten Salamence and must switch.
branches.then: Pressure with Salamence and consider Mega Evolution only when it creates immediate value.
branches.why: Do not give the opponent a free turn while preserving the Mega resource.

phases.title: Mid
phases.lede: Turn accumulated chip into the setup window your opponent cannot afford to give you.

branches.when: A Salamence answer is weakened or forced out.
branches.then: Bring Salamence into the favorable turn and set up.
branches.why: This is the primary conversion point.

branches.when: The opponent's faster threats are already weakened.
branches.why: Sucker Punch becomes increasingly difficult to play around.

phases.title: Late
phases.lede: Stop preserving pieces that no longer matter and finish with the correct priority or boosted attacker.

branches.when: The opponent has no safe answer to Mega Salamence.
branches.why: Do not give the opponent extra turns.

branches.when: The opponent has faster attackers remaining but must attack to win.
branches.then: Use Kingambit's Sucker Punch to close.
branches.why: Priority converts chip into a controlled endgame.

flows.title: Lead
flows.lede: Start by forcing the opponent to reveal how they intend to stop your core.

forks.when: They lead a physical attacker that Rotom-Wash handles.
forks.why: Cut the opponent's immediate damage before pivoting.

forks.when: The burned attacker remains in.
forks.then: Use Volt Switch if the opponent cannot punish the pivot.
forks.why: Bring Salamence into a weakened physical structure.

forks.when: The opponent switches to a Salamence answer.
forks.then: Attack or pivot according to the revealed answer.
forks.why: Bring the appropriate breaker into the newly revealed structure.

forks.when: Their lead cannot meaningfully threaten Salamence.
forks.then: Use Salamence to establish offensive pressure.
forks.why: Exploit the free matchup before the opponent can reposition.

forks.when: The opponent cannot punish a setup turn.
forks.why: Start the primary sweep.

forks.when: The opponent can punish setup but is vulnerable to Flying or Ground coverage.
forks.why: Take the guaranteed damage rather than gambling on setup.

flows.title: Mid
flows.lede: Turn the first favorable exchange into a controlled win-condition sequence.

forks.when: A Salamence answer is weakened or removed.
forks.then: Bring Salamence in and set up if safe.
forks.why: The opponent's structural answer has been removed.

forks.when: Salamence outspeeds the remaining threats after setup.
forks.then: Attack until the opponent's final Pokémon is forced into a losing exchange.
forks.why: Do not give the opponent a free recovery turn.

forks.when: The opponent's faster attackers are weakened and Kingambit can enter safely.
forks.why: The endgame is becoming favorable for priority.

forks.when: The opponent must switch or cannot meaningfully punish setup.
forks.why: Convert the favorable endgame into a direct sweep.

flows.title: Late
flows.lede: Choose the attack that prevents the opponent's last viable comeback route.

forks.when: The opposing Pokémon must attack and is in Sucker Punch range.
forks.why: Do not give a faster attacker a free turn.

forks.when: The opposing Pokémon can safely refuse to attack.
forks.why: Sucker Punch is unreliable against passive play.

forks.when: Mega Salamence has the remaining matchup under control.
forks.then: Keep attacking and use Roost only when recovery changes the outcome.
forks.why: End the battle before recoil or unnecessary turns create counterplay.

packs.label: Emergency Brake
packs.when: Their six contains multiple fast attackers, setup threats, or immediate offensive pressure.
packs.identity: Disguise plus defensive pivoting plus priority.

strategy.opponentPattern: Their six is built to overwhelm a slower balance core through speed, setup, or immediate offensive trades.
strategy.purpose: Mimikyu absorbs one critical interaction, Rotom-Wash disrupts physical pressure, and Kingambit controls the endgame with priority.
targets: Teams that rely on one primary sweeper
refuses: Do not bring this package when the opponent is overwhelmingly passive and gives Mimikyu little opportunity to exploit Disguise.
Do not rely on Kingambit's Sucker Punch if the opponent has several ways to refuse attacking.
strategy.winCondition: Survive the opponent's first offensive wave, use Mimikyu or Rotom-Wash to remove momentum, then let Kingambit clean.

pilot.thesis: Make the opponent spend their first wave of offense without allowing a clean sweep.
pilot.rule: Protect Mimikyu's Disguise until it creates a decisive interaction.
pilot.fail: If the opponent's offense is special-heavy and Rotom-Wash cannot absorb it, switch to the special-spam package.

packs.philosophy: Do not race hyper-offense turn for turn. Break its first wave, preserve one priority user, and make the opponent run out of clean attacks.
press: Preserve Disguise until it stops a real threat.
Burn physical attackers before they snowball.
Keep Kingambit healthy enough to finish.
refuse: Never throw Mimikyu into a minor hit just to reveal Disguise.
Never use Swords Dance with Mimikyu when the opponent can immediately overwhelm it afterward.
Never assume Sucker Punch wins if the opponent has safe status or setup options.

switches.send: Rotom-Wash to burn it before it can accumulate further pressure.
Kingambit when Sucker Punch can secure the trade.
Mimikyu to exploit Disguise and force a direct interaction.

plan.title: Clock
plan.goal: Stop the opponent from snowballing immediately.
plan.play: Use Rotom-Wash to burn physical threats and Mimikyu to absorb the one attack that would otherwise break the structure.
plan.next: Preserve whichever piece the opponent still cannot safely answer.

plan.title: Shield
plan.goal: Prevent the opponent from retaining three functional attackers.
plan.play: Trade Mimikyu only for a meaningful threat and use Rotom-Wash to deny physical setup.
plan.next: Bring Kingambit into the weakened offensive field.

plan.title: Clean
plan.goal: Use priority to stop the final offensive threat.
plan.play: Sucker Punch weakened faster attackers and use Kowtow Cleave when they refuse to attack.
plan.next: Do not overpredict when a direct KO is available.

loops.title: Disguise Loop
loops.body: Keep Mimikyu hidden until the opponent commits to the attack you need Disguise to absorb, then convert the protected turn into a KO or setup.

loops.title: Burn Loop
loops.body: Rotom-Wash burns the physical attacker, pivots out, and returns later when the opponent tries to restore offensive pressure.

packs.label: Bully Core
packs.when: Their six contains passive walls, Steel-heavy structures, or obvious Salamence answers that Garchomp can attack immediately.
packs.identity: Immediate coverage pressure with two physical breakers and a Mega finisher.

strategy.opponentPattern: Their six relies on defensive cores, slower Steel answers, or predictable switches to survive conventional offensive pressure.
strategy.purpose: Garchomp attacks immediately with four coverage moves, Salamence threatens setup, and Kingambit punishes the weakened endgame.
targets: Teams with weak immediate answers to Ground and Fire coverage
refuses: Do not bring this package when the opponent has several strong Ice attackers.
Do not bring it when their physical walls comfortably stop all three attackers.
strategy.winCondition: Use Garchomp's coverage to remove or weaken defensive answers, then let Mega Salamence or Kingambit finish.

pilot.thesis: Do not give passive structures free turns; attack the switch they need.
pilot.rule: Use Garchomp's coverage before giving the opponent time to stabilize.
pilot.fail: If their physical shell survives repeated direct attacks, stop feeding it physical attackers and choose the special-spam package.

packs.philosophy: This package sacrifices some defensive flexibility for immediate offensive compression.
press: Attack the predicted Steel switch with Fire Fang.
Use Earthquake when the opponent has no safe Ground immunity.
Preserve Kingambit until the opponent's physical answers are weakened.
refuse: Never send Garchomp into known Ice pressure.
Never Dragon Dance Salamence into an obvious immediate revenge KO.
Never sacrifice Kingambit while Fairy targets remain important.

switches.send: Garchomp with Fire Fang or Earthquake according to typing.
Salamence when its other weaknesses are not exposed.

plan.title: Clock

plan.next: Record which Pokémon they rely on to stop Ground, Dragon, Flying, and Dark pressure.

plan.title: Shield
plan.goal: Preserve the attacker that the opponent still cannot answer.
plan.play: Do not trade both breakers into the same defensive wall.
plan.next: Use the surviving breaker to create the endgame.

plan.title: Clean
plan.goal: Finish after the defensive structure has been cracked.
plan.play: Mega Salamence sweeps if its checks are gone; Kingambit cleans if faster threats are weakened.
plan.next: Choose the win condition based on what remains, not what you planned at preview.

hazards.rule: If Ice pressure is central to their six, use a different pack.

Preserve Kingambit until its priority can end the game.

Rotom-Wash or Rillaboom according to the opponent's coverage.

pilot.rule: Never select the same three automatically; first identify the opponent's biggest pressure point and your cleanest answer to it.

press: Read their six before choosing your three.
Identify their strongest win condition and their answer to yours.
Use Rotom-Wash to create controlled entries when it is part of the package.

advantages.title: Six-to-three compression
advantages.body: The roster contains three distinct packages rather than one fixed trio: balanced control, anti-offense, and direct physical pressure.
advantages.watch: Do not confuse the roster's strongest six with the correct three for every preview.
advantages.play: Select the package that attacks the opponent's structure.

advantages.title: Multiple endgames
advantages.body: Mega Salamence, Kingambit, and Mimikyu can all serve as different closing mechanisms depending on which opposing checks are removed.
advantages.watch: Do not preserve every attacker equally.
advantages.play: Identify the one Pokémon that the opponent has the fewest answers to.
advantages.rule: Protect the least replaceable win condition.

hazards.title: Shared Dragon exposure
hazards.body: Salamence and Garchomp both become difficult to use when the opponent has strong Ice pressure.
hazards.watch: Identify every strong Ice attack before selecting a package containing both.
hazards.play: Use Rotom-Wash, Kingambit, or Mimikyu to change the matchup instead.
hazards.rule: Do not stack Dragon vulnerabilities without a concrete reason.

hazards.title: Priority wars
hazards.body: Kingambit, Mimikyu, and Rillaboom all rely partly on priority to control endgames.
hazards.watch: Track opposing priority and Ghost or Dark interactions before assuming a priority move is safe.
hazards.play: Use direct attacks when the opponent can manipulate priority.
hazards.rule: Priority is a closing tool, not an automatic first choice.

hazards.title: Mega resource
hazards.body: Mega Salamence is the team's dedicated Mega option, so selecting it does not mean Mega Evolution should happen immediately.
hazards.watch: Ask whether the Mega changes the current matchup or merely adds power you could obtain later.
hazards.play: Preserve the Mega option until the opponent's structure is understood.
hazards.rule: Mega for the win condition, not for habit.

training.why: Maximize physical damage while investing enough Speed to improve the value of Dragon Dance without abandoning useful bulk.

28 Spe — make Dragon Dance convert Salamence into a decisive cleaner.

slots.objective: Create one safe Dragon Dance opportunity, then convert the resulting speed and power into a decisive endgame.
slots.howToPlay:
Do not Mega automatically.
Use Intimidate to create a safer entry when possible.
Do not Dragon Dance while the opponent still has an obvious faster revenge killer unless the trade is favorable.
Use Double-Edge to punish neutral targets and Earthquake to punish Steel or Electric answers.
Roost when recoil or chip would prevent Salamence from reaching the endgame.
Preserve Salamence if it is your only reliable route through the opponent's remaining structure.

slots.title: The Circuit Breaker
slots.role: Use Rotom-Wash to absorb physical pressure, burn attackers, and create safe entries for Salamence or Kingambit.
slots.itemWhy: Provide immediate recovery after taking a hit and let Rotom-Wash repeatedly perform its pivot and disruption role.

itemAlts.name: Leftovers
itemAlts.why: Prefer this when the game is expected to involve many turns of switching rather than one critical burst of recovery.

itemAlts.name: Choice Scarf
itemAlts.why: Prefer this only when immediate Speed and revenge pressure are more valuable than defensive utility.

spend: 32 HP — maximize general durability.
24 Def — strengthen the physical matchups Rotom-Wash is assigned to check.
10 SpA — retain offensive pressure with Hydro Pump and Thunderbolt.

alts.name: Specially Durable

spend: 32 HP — maximize general durability.
16 SpD — improve special resilience.
10 Def — retain physical utility.

moves.name: Volt Switch
moves.why: Turn favorable matchups into controlled entries for Salamence, Kingambit, or another selected teammate.

alts.name: Thunderbolt
alts.why: Use when staying in and dealing direct Electric damage is more important than pivoting.

moves.name: Hydro Pump
moves.why: Give Rotom-Wash strong Water STAB against Ground, Fire, Rock, and other targets that expect passive play.

alts.name: Surf
alts.why: Use when accuracy matters more than peak damage into a known stay.

moves.name: Will-O-Wisp
moves.why: Cut physical pressure and make opposing attackers easier for the rest of the team to handle.

alts.name: Thunder Wave

moves.name: Thunderbolt
moves.why: Provide direct Electric pressure when pivoting is unnecessary or when a Water or Flying target must be threatened immediately.

alts.name: Protect

slots.objective: Create safe turns and stop the opponent from freely attacking while keeping the correct breaker healthy.
slots.howToPlay:
Lead Rotom-Wash when the preview shows an immediate physical threat it can comfortably disrupt.
Click Will-O-Wisp against physical attackers unless the burn is clearly exploitable by the opponent.
Use Volt Switch when the opponent must respect Hydro Pump or Electric pressure.
Do not sacrifice Rotom-Wash merely to chip something unless the remaining two can exploit the opening.
Use Hydro Pump when the opponent expects a passive Volt Switch.
Preserve Rotom-Wash when it is your safest answer to the opponent's main physical breaker.

slots.title: The Guillotine
slots.role: Use Kingambit as the team's endgame cleaner and punish weakened teams with Supreme Overlord and priority.
slots.itemWhy: Increase the damage of Kingambit's Dark attacks without locking it into a move and make Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave threatening after setup or teammate losses.

itemAlts.name: Lum Berry
itemAlts.why: Prefer this when status is more dangerous than maximizing Dark-type damage.

itemAlts.name: Leftovers
itemAlts.why: Prefer this in slower games where repeated switching and passive recovery matter.

training.label: Bulky Blade
training.why: Maximize Attack and give Kingambit enough HP to survive longer while retaining a small amount of special bulk.
spend: 32 HP — maximize general durability.
32 Atk — maximize Sucker Punch, Kowtow Cleave, and Iron Head damage.
2 SpD — place the remaining SP into special bulk.

alts.name: Speed Utility
alts.why: Prefer this when creeping slower defensive threats is more valuable than maximum bulk.
spend: 32 Atk — maximize damage.
22 HP — retain meaningful bulk.
12 Spe — improve positioning against slower targets.

moves.name: Sucker Punch

alts.name: Low Kick
alts.why: Use when opposing Kingambit and heavy Steel targets are more important than priority.

alts.name: Night Slash

moves.name: Swords Dance

alts.name: Stealth Rock
alts.why: Use when Kingambit is being deployed primarily as a utility lead rather than a cleaner.

moves.name: Iron Head
moves.why: Provide Steel STAB for Fairy targets and prevent Fairy Pokémon from freely absorbing Dark attacks.

alts.name: Low Kick

slots.objective: Survive long enough for the opponent's team to become weakened, then use Supreme Overlord and priority to close the game.
slots.howToPlay:
Do not expose Kingambit early without a reason.
Use Sucker Punch only when the opponent must attack.
Use Kowtow Cleave when you expect a switch or status move.
Swords Dance when the opponent gives you a genuinely passive turn.
Preserve Kingambit if faster offensive Pokémon remain healthy.
Treat the final opposing Pokémon as the ideal Supreme Overlord target.
